password_security_checkup.marketingCopy: Weak, reused, or previously leaked passwords are the single most common way small businesses get breached. The Password Security Checkup gives you a practical audit of how your company actually handles credentials today. We review your Microsoft 365 password policies, scan your business email domain against the HaveIBeenPwned breach database to see which accounts have been exposed, document shared logins and generic mailboxes that create accountability gaps, and assess whether a business password manager like Bitwarden, 1Password, or Keeper is the right fit. You receive a plain-English scorecard and a prioritized list of fixes you can act on immediately, plus a 30-minute walkthrough so you fully understand what we found and what to do next.
bestFor: Businesses that reuse the same password across multiple accounts or systems
Companies where staff share login credentials through spreadsheets or chat
Organizations that have never reviewed their password policies or breached-account exposure
Businesses applying for cyber insurance that need evidence of password hygiene
whatIsIncluded: Full password policy audit across Microsoft 365 and known cloud platforms
Domain-wide compromised-credential scan using the HaveIBeenPwned API
Shared account and generic mailbox inventory with risk assessment
Password manager readiness evaluation comparing Bitwarden, 1Password, and Keeper
Plain-English Password Security Scorecard with prioritized recommendations
30-minute customer walkthrough of findings and next steps
customerOutcomes: A clear, documented picture of your password posture across every business system
Knowledge of exactly which business accounts have been exposed in known breaches
A prioritized, low-effort plan for eliminating weak, shared, and reused credentials
Credible password hygiene evidence you can submit with cyber insurance applications

mfa_setup_session.marketingCopy: Multi-factor authentication stops more than 99% of automated account-takeover attacks, yet most small businesses still rely on a password alone for email, banking, payroll, and cloud apps. The MFA Setup Session audits every critical business account for MFA coverage, then configures it hands-on where you have admin access. We enforce MFA with a Microsoft 365 Conditional Access policy so it applies to every user automatically, enable Google Workspace 2-Step Verification when applicable, and walk you through securing third-party platforms like your domain registrar, payroll provider, and banking portals. Every user gets clear enrollment instructions, we verify sign-in works across phone and desktop apps, and we document recovery codes safely so nobody gets permanently locked out.
bestFor: Businesses that don't have MFA enabled on email, banking, payroll, or cloud accounts
Organizations whose cyber insurance now requires MFA across all critical accounts
Companies that need hands-on help enabling MFA without confusing technical documentation
Businesses that recently suffered an email or account compromise and want it to stop happening
whatIsIncluded: Audit of all business-critical accounts to identify MFA gaps
Microsoft 365 MFA configuration with a Conditional Access policy that applies to every user
Google Workspace 2-Step Verification setup when applicable
Guided MFA enablement for third-party platforms (banking, payroll, CRM, domain registrar)
Authenticator app enrollment and training for all users with recovery code storage
Post-configuration sign-in testing on every platform we secure
customerOutcomes: MFA enforced on email, cloud apps, and every critical third-party account we can reach
A Conditional Access policy in Microsoft 365 that blocks sign-ins without a second factor
Staff enrolled and comfortable using an authenticator app with no lockouts or confusion
Documented MFA status per platform that satisfies insurance and audit requests

phishing_readiness_mini_audit.marketingCopy: Phishing is the attack path behind most real-world business breaches, and the question every owner asks is: would my staff actually recognize it? The Phishing Readiness Mini Audit gives you a fast, evidence-based answer. We review your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records so we know whether someone can spoof your domain, audit your Microsoft 365 anti-phishing and anti-spam settings, scan user mailboxes for suspicious forwarding rules that indicate a takeover, and optionally run a safe, controlled phishing simulation to measure real click and report rates. You get a clear scorecard of your email defenses and your team's awareness, with specific fixes ranked by impact.
bestFor: Businesses that receive phishing emails and want to know whether staff would fall for them
Organizations that have never reviewed their email authentication or anti-phishing settings
Companies preparing for cyber insurance that asks about phishing awareness testing
Businesses that experienced a phishing-related compromise or near-miss and want a baseline
whatIsIncluded: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC record audit to detect spoofable email domains
Microsoft 365 anti-phishing policy review including impersonation protection
Microsoft 365 anti-spam and quarantine settings review
Mailbox forwarding-rule audit to spot signs of account compromise
Optional controlled phishing simulation with click, report, and reply metrics
Phishing Readiness Scorecard with prioritized remediation steps
customerOutcomes: A clear picture of whether your email domain can be impersonated and how to stop it
Measured staff phishing awareness compared against realistic expectations
Specific Microsoft 365 settings changes that meaningfully reduce phishing risk
An actionable scorecard you can reuse to track awareness improvements over time

security_score_snapshot.marketingCopy: Most small businesses have never had a formal security assessment, so they guess where the risk is instead of knowing. The Security Score Snapshot replaces guesswork with a single number you can track. We evaluate five domains that matter most for a small organization - identity, endpoints, email, backup, and admin access - against practical baseline controls, then score you 0 to 100. Each domain gets a red, amber, or green rating with the specific evidence behind it, and we finish with your top five quick-win fixes ranked by risk reduction versus effort. This is a fast, affordable baseline you can rerun quarterly to prove you're improving, and it produces exactly the kind of evidence cyber insurers want to see.
bestFor: Business owners who want an objective, measurable security score rather than gut feeling
Organizations that have never had any security assessment and need a starting baseline
Companies applying for cyber insurance that need a gap list and improvement evidence
Businesses that want to measure security improvement over time with a repeatable score
whatIsIncluded: Identity review: MFA coverage, admin accounts, and shared credential risk
Endpoint review: protection software, patch status, encryption, and local admin rights
Email review: SPF/DKIM/DMARC, anti-phishing policy, and mailbox-rule risk
Backup review: configuration, success history, retention, and off-site copy
Admin access review: privileged accounts, stale accounts, and excessive permissions
Security Scorecard with an overall 0-100 score and five prioritized quick wins
customerOutcomes: A clear 0-100 security score you can benchmark and track over time
Red, amber, and green ratings across the five domains that drive most small-business risk
Five prioritized actions ranked by risk reduction versus implementation effort
Repeatable, insurance-ready evidence of your security posture

admin_account_cleanup.marketingCopy: Every former employee, past IT provider, and abandoned project usually leaves behind an admin account - and each one is a back door into your business. The Admin Account Cleanup finds and removes them. We audit privileged access across Microsoft 365, on-premises Active Directory when present, and cloud platforms like Google Workspace, Salesforce, and QuickBooks. We identify stale accounts for departed staff, shared admin logins with no individual accountability, and users whose privileges exceed their job. You approve every change before we make it, and you end up with a documented, least-privilege admin structure with clear ownership for every account that remains.
bestFor: Businesses that have gone through employee turnover or IT-provider changes without cleaning up access
Organizations that still rely on shared admin logins with no way to know who used them
Companies where nobody is sure who currently has administrative privileges
Businesses preparing for an audit, compliance review, or cyber insurance application
whatIsIncluded: Microsoft 365 admin account audit covering Global, Exchange, SharePoint, and Teams admins
On-premises Active Directory admin group review when applicable
Cloud platform admin audit across Google Workspace, Salesforce, QuickBooks, and more
Stale and shared account identification with risk documentation
Approved removal or demotion of unnecessary privileges with audit logging
Final admin inventory documenting ownership, purpose, and review date for every account
customerOutcomes: A complete inventory of every administrative account across your business platforms
Former-employee, shared, and unused admin access removed with documented approval
A least-privilege admin structure where each account maps to a person and a job
Dramatically reduced risk of insider misuse and post-termination access

business_email_safety_check.marketingCopy: Your business email is your digital front door, and if SPF, DKIM, and DMARC aren't configured correctly, anyone can send emails that appear to come from you. The Business Email Safety Check verifies your domain's email authentication, reviews your Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace security settings, audits every mailbox's forwarding rules for unauthorized exfiltration, and confirms MFA is actually enabled on email accounts. It catches the exact failures that lead to business email compromise, spam-flagged domains that hurt deliverability, and silent data leaks through forwarding. You get a straight-to-the-point report with the specific records and settings that need fixing.
bestFor: Businesses worried about scammers impersonating their domain to customers and partners
Organizations whose legitimate emails are landing in spam due to missing authentication
Companies that want to verify nobody has set up unauthorized mailbox forwarding
Businesses preparing for cyber insurance that requires verified email authentication
whatIsIncluded: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC record audit with deliverability and spoofing implications
Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace email security configuration review
Mailbox forwarding-rule audit across all user mailboxes
MFA status verification on all email accounts
Anti-spoofing and anti-impersonation configuration recommendations
Plain-English email security report with prioritized fixes
customerOutcomes: Verified SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configuration that blocks domain spoofing
Discovery and removal of any unauthorized email forwarding or data-exfiltration rules
Confirmation that MFA protects every mailbox, closing the most common BEC path
Improved email deliverability because authentication records are correct

remote_work_safety_check.marketingCopy: Remote work moves your business network into home offices, coffee shops, and personal devices - and most companies never formally reviewed what that exposed. The Remote Work Safety Check evaluates how your staff actually connect and work remotely. We review your VPN and remote-desktop configuration for unsafe exposure, check whether MFA protects remote access, assess device policies like disk encryption and patching on laptops, and flag risky practices like personal devices handling business data or unsecured home Wi-Fi. You get a practical assessment of your remote-work risk with concrete changes you can make this week.
bestFor: Businesses with employees working from home, in the field, or on the road
Organizations that allow personal devices or home networks to touch business data
Companies that use VPN, Remote Desktop, or cloud apps for remote access
Businesses that scaled up remote work quickly and never audited the security implications
whatIsIncluded: Remote access infrastructure review covering VPN, RDP, and management tools
MFA coverage verification for all remote access paths
Device posture assessment: encryption, antivirus, patching, and local admin rights
Guidance on home Wi-Fi security and personal device use for remote staff
Remote work policy review with practical improvement recommendations
Remote Work Safety Report with findings and prioritized actions
customerOutcomes: A clear picture of every way employees access business systems remotely
Unsafe remote-access exposures identified and prioritized for immediate fixing
Concrete guidance staff can follow to secure home networks and personal devices

basic_incident_readiness_checklist.marketingCopy: When a security incident happens, panic and hesitation cause more damage than the attack itself. The Basic Incident Readiness Checklist gives your team a simple, usable playbook before something goes wrong. We build a step-by-step first-response checklist customized to your business size and systems: who does what, who to call, and how to contain the four most common scenarios - email compromise, ransomware, data breach, and service outage. This isn't a 50-page policy binder; it's a laminated, real-world checklist your staff can actually follow at 3 a.m. during an incident, and it satisfies the incident-response requirements many cyber insurers now demand.
bestFor: Businesses that have no incident response plan and want a practical starting point
Organizations that need a usable checklist rather than a dense policy document
Companies whose cyber insurance requires evidence of incident response readiness
Small teams that want clear roles and phone numbers defined before an emergency
whatIsIncluded: Incident classification guide with realistic examples for your business
Defined roles: incident commander, communications lead, and technical lead
Emergency contact list template covering insurance, legal, IT, and law enforcement
Step-by-step containment procedures for email compromise, ransomware, breach, and outage
Containment checklist covering isolate, preserve, notify, and begin recovery
Post-incident review template for lessons learned and improvements
customerOutcomes: A customized first-response checklist your team can execute under pressure
Clear roles, ownership, and escalation contacts defined before an incident happens
Faster containment in the critical first hour when decisions matter most
Incident-readiness documentation accepted by cyber insurance applications

website_uptime_monitor_setup.marketingCopy: A down website silently costs you leads, sales, and credibility - and most small businesses only find out when a customer calls. The Website Uptime Monitor Setup puts automated monitoring on your site so you know about problems before your customers do. We configure a professional uptime service that checks your site from multiple global locations every few minutes, alert you by email, SMS, or Slack when it goes down, and tune the alert rules so you aren't woken up by false alarms. We test that alerts actually fire, document the whole setup, and hand you a working early-warning system for your most important sales tool.
bestFor: Businesses whose website drives leads, bookings, sales, or customer inquiries
Organizations that have discovered downtime from customers instead of from monitoring
Companies that want automated uptime alerts without managing the tooling themselves
Businesses that rely on a client portal, quote form, or e-commerce checkout being online
whatIsIncluded: Uptime monitoring service selection and configuration (UptimeRobot, BetterStack, or similar)
Multi-location monitoring for global coverage of your website
Email, SMS, and Slack or Teams alert routing
Alert-rule tuning to prevent false positives and alert fatigue
Monitoring setup documentation with escalation contacts
Initial monitoring and alert-testing period to confirm everything fires correctly
customerOutcomes: Automated downtime detection within minutes, from multiple locations worldwide
Instant alerts through the channels your team actually watches
Fewer false alarms because rules are tuned to your site's real behavior
Peace of mind that website issues are caught before customers complain

printer_scanner_setup.marketingCopy: A printer that won't print or a scanner that won't scan is one of the most common daily frustrations in a small office - and usually a 20-minute fix hiding behind a confusing driver error. The Printer or Scanner Setup service handles it end to end. We connect the device to your network over wired or wireless, install the correct drivers on every workstation that needs access, configure scan-to-email or scan-to-folder so scanning actually saves time, set sensible defaults like duplex and paper size, and test printing and scanning from every machine so nothing is left half-working. Your team gets a device that just works, plus simple instructions for the tasks they do every day.
bestFor: Offices with a new printer or scanner that needs professional network setup
Businesses where printing or scanning only works on some computers
Companies that want scan-to-email or scan-to-folder configured properly
Teams tired of troubleshooting the same printer error on every workstation
whatIsIncluded: Wired or wireless network configuration for the printer or scanner
Driver installation and configuration on all designated workstations
Scan-to-email, scan-to-folder, or scan-to-cloud destination setup
Print queue, default settings, and duplex configuration
Functionality testing from every workstation including test prints and test scans
Simple user instructions for common printing and scanning tasks
customerOutcomes: Printing and scanning that work reliably from every designated workstation
Scan-to-email and scan-to-folder saving time instead of creating workarounds

pc_tune_up_cleanup.marketingCopy: Slow computers aren't a hardware problem as often as you'd think - they're usually a build-up of startup programs, junk files, outdated software, and bloatware. The PC Tune-Up and Cleanup service gives a sluggish workstation a measurable performance boost without spending thousands on new hardware. We clear temporary files and old downloads, disable unnecessary startup items that slow boot times, install pending Windows and application updates, remove software nobody uses, and benchmark the machine before and after so you can see the real improvement in boot time, available memory, and disk speed. For a business extending the life of existing computers, this is the cheapest performance upgrade available.
bestFor: Businesses with workstations that have gotten noticeably slower over time
Organizations that want to extend the life of existing hardware before buying replacements
Staff members frustrated by long boot times and sluggish everyday performance
Companies that want measurable before-and-after proof of a performance fix
whatIsIncluded: Disk analysis and cleanup of temporary files, old downloads, and recycle bin contents
Startup program review and optimization for faster boot times
Installation of pending Windows and application updates
Identification and removal of unnecessary or bloatware software
Before-and-after performance benchmarking (boot time, memory, disk speed)
Maintenance recommendations to keep the machine fast
customerOutcomes: Measurably faster boot and everyday performance with benchmark proof
Recovered disk space from files and applications that were never needed
A cleaner, more secure system with updates and fewer attack surfaces
Extended useful life for existing hardware, delaying replacement spending

computer_replacement_readiness_review.marketingCopy: Replacing business computers without a plan means emergency purchases, inconsistent hardware, and budget surprises. The Computer Replacement Readiness Review turns that scramble into a predictable roadmap. We audit your entire computer fleet - age, specifications, performance, and warranty status - and sort every device into one of three buckets: replace now, extend with an upgrade, or fine for now. You get a prioritized replacement list with specific model recommendations at budget, standard, and performance tiers, a multi-year budget projection, and guidance on data transfer and secure disposal of retired devices. It's hardware lifecycle management for businesses that can't afford to guess.
bestFor: Businesses planning to refresh aging computers and unsure what to replace first
Organizations that want to budget for hardware over multiple years instead of scrambling
Companies with a mixed-age fleet that needs standardization
Businesses that want to stop making reactive, emergency computer purchases
whatIsIncluded: Complete fleet audit: age, specifications, performance, and warranty status per device
Replacement priority ranking with clear reasoning for each computer
Model recommendations at budget, standard, and performance tiers
Three-year budget projection for hardware refresh
Data transfer planning guidance for the replacement process
Secure disposal recommendations for retired devices
customerOutcomes: A prioritized, honest list of which computers must be replaced now versus later
A multi-year hardware budget you can plan around instead of react to
Standardized device recommendations that reduce support complexity
Clear handling of retired devices including secure wipe and recycling options
